brief: Hot September CPI and PPI pushed October Fed hike odds above 50%, but AI's financing problem then dominated the week: CoreWeave bonds fell into distress, hedge funds dumped AI exposure added since January 2025, the Kospi entered a bear market and the Nasdaq 100 had its worst week since Liberation Day. The 10Y fell to a three-week low near 5.09%, Fed's Warsh gave no October guidance, and hike odds collapsed to 14%. As sentiment cooled, BofA's Bull & Bear Indicator dropped to 7.4 from 8.1, ending the May 26 sell signal, which Hartnett stresses is not a buy signal: FMS positioning is still 100th-percentile bullish and 2026 equity and tech inflows remain record-pace despite the AI crack. Hartnett therefore stays risk-off for the next 3-4 weeks, citing 2.9% real yields nearing the 3% level historically tied to market breaks, the need for an October 28 hike, and stress among AI lenders (PSP and BIZD at lows, Oracle's CDS parabolic). Goldman's Curtin separately argues higher yields are cracking sub-investment-grade AI financing, with hyperscaler capex outrunning cash flow. Hartnett's 2027 call: semiconductor prices, now vertical, will decide whether AI credit stays open or tightens.
